name: Question 6
worked_solution:
The gradient of the function $f(x,y,z)$ is defined as

$$
∇f(x,y,z)=\frac{∂f}{∂x}\,i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\,j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}\,k.
$$

Since $∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z),$ the function $f(x,y,z)$ must satisfy the following system:

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂x}=2xz+\operatorname{sin}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂f}{∂z}={x}^{2}
$$

First, we integrate $\frac{∂f}{∂x}$ with respect to $x.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $y$ and $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =\int \frac{∂f}{∂x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\int (2xz+\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={x}^{2}z+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+g(y,z)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to $y,$ we obtain

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\frac{∂g}{∂y}
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂y}=x\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}x\operatorname{cos}⁡y+\frac{∂g}{∂y} & =x\operatorname{cos}⁡y \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate $\frac{∂g}{∂y}$ with respect to $y.$ Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of $z:$

$$
\begin{aligned}g(y,z) & =\int \frac{∂g}{∂y}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\int 0\,\text{d}y \\  & =h(z)\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $g(y,z)=h(z)$ in the expression for $f(x,y,z),$ we get

$$
f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+h(z).
$$

To determine the function $h(z),$ we differentiate $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $z.$ This gives

$$
\frac{∂f}{∂z}={x}^{2}+{h}^{′}(z).
$$

Taking $\frac{∂f}{∂z}={x}^{2}$ into account, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2} & ={x}^{2}+{h}^{′}(z) \\ {h}^{′}(z) & =0 \\ h(z) & =C,\end{aligned}
$$

where $C$ is a constant.

Consequently,

$$
f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}z+x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+C.
$$

Question 6
?

Find f(x,y,z) such that ∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z), where F(x,y,z)=(2xz+sin⁡y)i+xcos⁡yj+x2k.

a
 f(x,y,z)=x2z+xsin⁡y+C
b
 f(x,y,z)=x2z2+x2cos⁡y+C
c
 f(x,y,z)=xy+x2z+sin⁡y+C
d
 f(x,y,z)=xy2−zcos⁡y+C
e
 f(x,y,z)=x2+yz+xsin⁡y+C
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The gradient of the function f(x,y,z) is defined as ∇f(x,y,z)=∂f∂xi+∂f∂yj+∂f∂zk.

Since ∇f(x,y,z)=F(x,y,z), the function f(x,y,z) must satisfy the following system: ∂f∂x=2xz+sin⁡y,∂f∂y=xcos⁡y,∂f∂z=x2

First, we integrate ∂f∂x with respect to x. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of y and z: f(x,y,z)=∫∂f∂xdx=∫(2xz+sin⁡y)dx=x2z+xsin⁡y+g(y,z)

Now, differentiating the above expression with respect to y, we obtain ∂f∂y=xcos⁡y+∂g∂y

Taking ∂f∂y=xcos⁡y into account, we obtain

xcos⁡y+∂g∂y=xcos⁡y∂g∂y=0

Now, we integrate ∂g∂y with respect to y. Note that the solution should contain an arbitrary function of z: g(y,z)=∫∂g∂ydy=∫0dy=h(z)

Substituting g(y,z)=h(z) in the expression for f(x,y,z), we get f(x,y,z)=x2z+xsin⁡y+h(z).

To determine the function h(z), we differentiate f(x,y,z) with respect to z. This gives ∂f∂z=x2+h′(z).

Taking ∂f∂z=x2 into account, we obtain x2=x2+h′(z)h′(z)=0h(z)=C, where C is a constant.

Consequently, f(x,y,z)=x2z+xsin⁡y+C.
